title: A Probabilistic Hard Concept Bottleneck for Steerable Generative Models
claim: A generic generative model with a concept bottleneck is refined by a probabilistic hard-concept layer that splits concept and unsupervised latents.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, (b) zooms into the bottleneck block of (a)
description: Two block diagrams separated by a dashed vertical line. Panel (a) shows a gray rounded box labeled Concept Bottleneck Generative Model. Inside, a noisy input u flows through a blue Pre Bottleneck Module, then a white Concept Bottleneck box, then a blue Post Bottleneck Module. These produce the embeddings w and ŵ, and the output is a face photo x. Panel (b) zooms into the bottleneck as Variational Hard Concept Bottleneck. An input w enters a purple Encoder g_η(w), which splits into two branches. The top branch gives concepts c from q_η(c|w), drawn as green binary vectors. The bottom branch gives an unsupervised representation s from q_η(s|w), drawn as orange binary vectors. An ECC step expands each into v_c and v_s. Soft modulation then produces z_c, and the two branches are concatenated into z. A purple Decoder f_θ(z) outputs ŵ. Green and orange color-code the supervised and unsupervised paths.
caption: Block diagram of (a) the general architecture of CBGMs, and (b) the VHCB layer. Note that the Error-Correcting Code (ECC) in the VHCB layer is a deterministic transformation that enables effective inference.
abstract: Concept Bottleneck Generative Models (CBGMs) incorporate a human-interpretable concept bottleneck layer, which makes them interpretable and steerable. However, designing such a layer for generative models poses the same challenges as for concept bottleneck models in a supervised context, if not greater ones. Deterministic mappings from the model inner representations to soft concepts in existing CBGMs: (i) limit steerable generation to modifying concepts in existing inputs; and, more importantly, (ii) are susceptible to concept leakage , which hinders their steerability. To address these limitations, we first introduce the Variational Hard Concept Bottleneck (VHCB) layer. The VHCB maps probabilistic estimates of binary latent variables to hard concepts, which have been shown to mitigate leakage. Remarkably, its probabilistic formulation enables direct generation from a specified set of concepts. Second, we propose a systematic evaluation framework for assessing the steerability of CBGMs across various tasks (e.g., activating and deactivating concepts). Our framework which allows us to empirically demonstrate that the VHCB layer consistently improves steerability.
